targets.question: Let my AI generate speech and manage voice agents with my ElevenLabs account

pick.name: ElevenLabs hosted MCP server

access.scope_note: Endpoint https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp (regional variants for EU, India, Singapore residency). OAuth consent asks for 'ElevenAgents read and write operations' and 'Text to Speech', limited to the workspace you sign in with. Tools: create, update, duplicate and delete agents; list and inspect agent configs; read conversations and transcripts; explore conversation topics; estimate LLM cost; fetch widget config and share links; check knowledge base size; generate speech with short-lived download links. Per-tool enable/disable and require-approval toggles exist in the client, and workspace admins can configure the connector for everyone.

clients: any client supporting OAuth with hosted client metadata
pick.cost: Server is free. Every generation burns ElevenLabs credits from your plan; the free tier is 10k credits a month.
pick.the_catch: It is an agents server with TTS bolted on. Voice cloning, speech-to-text, voice isolation, sound effects, music and dubbing, the things people actually wanted from the old local server, are not in the hosted tool list. Meanwhile ElevenLabs has stamped 'deprecated' on the local server that does have them (see alternate). Delete agent is one tool call and destructive; turn approval on for it. Data-residency workspaces must use the regional URL or auth fails.

alternate.name: elevenlabs-mcp (local, deprecated)

access.scope_note: 24 tools: text-to-speech, speech-to-text, voice cloning and voice design, speech-to-speech, audio isolation, sound effects, music (Music v2), video-to-music, agent creation, knowledge base upload, outbound calls. Runs as uvx elevenlabs-mcp with ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, so it has whatever the key has: there are no scopes. ELEVENLABS_MCP_BASE_PATH (default ~/Desktop) is both the output folder and the boundary for any local file a tool reads; paths outside are rejected. ELEVENLABS_MCP_OUTPUT_MODE picks files, MCP resources, or both.

alternate.cost: Free, MIT. Every call spends ElevenLabs credits; the README warns you before the tool list.
alternate.the_catch: The README's first line now says this server is deprecated in favour of the hosted one, yet v0.12.2 shipped on 4 Aug 2026 and it still does far more audio work than the hosted server. Expect it to stop getting features, not to stop working. Your full API key sits in the client config in plain text. Voice design and isolation calls can take long enough to hit client timeouts.

targets.avoid: mamertofabian/elevenlabs-mcp-server and various forks named 'The official ElevenLabs MCP server' are not ElevenLabs. The official ones are under github.com/elevenlabs and the hosted endpoint on api.elevenlabs.io.

targets.question: Let my AI read my Figma designs and draw on the canvas

pick.name: Figma MCP Server (remote)

access.scope_note: Read side: get_design_context (React + Tailwind representation of a selection), get_variable_defs, get_metadata, get_screenshot, plus FigJam and Make resources and Code Connect maps. Write side (remote server only): create and modify frames, components, variables and auto layout, create_new_file. No dedicated delete tool is documented, but write tools edit real files with no dry-run. You can only reach files your Figma account can already view or edit; there is no narrower scope than your own permissions. Endpoint https://mcp.figma.com/mcp, OAuth in the browser. The desktop server (runs inside the Figma app, Dev/Full seat on a paid plan) is read-only in comparison.

pick.cost: Free during beta. Figma says outright it 'will eventually be a usage-based paid feature'.
pick.the_catch: Rate limits are per seat, and they are brutal at the bottom. A View or Collab seat on a paid plan gets 6 tool calls a month (20 on Starter). Dev or Full seats get 200/day at 10/min on Professional, 200/day at 15/min on Organization, 600/day at 20/min on Enterprise. A single design-to-code pass can be several calls, so a View seat is effectively unusable. Second bite: only clients in Figma's MCP Catalog may connect at all; anything else is refused server-side, no waitlist skip. Third: write-to-canvas is beta and edits the live file. Version history is your undo.

alternate.name: Framelink Figma MCP (figma-developer-mcp)

access.scope_note: Read-only. Fetches layout and style data for a file or node via the REST API and simplifies it for the model; can download images. Uses a Figma personal access token (FIGMA_API_KEY), so it sees whatever files that token's account can see. No canvas writes at all.

alternate.cost: Free, MIT. Runs via npx. Figma REST API quotas apply to your token.
alternate.the_catch: It goes through the Figma REST API with a PAT, so it is bound by REST rate limits and Figma's own plan rules for the REST API, not the MCP limits. Read-only means it cannot draw. And it is a random GitHub user's project with 15k stars, not Figma's; the npm package name figma-developer-mcp looks official and is not.

targets.avoid: The npm registry has a dozen packages called some variant of figma-mcp. None are Figma's. Figma does not publish an npm package; the official server is the hosted endpoint at mcp.figma.com or the one built into the desktop app.

sources.label: Figma help centre guide (beta pricing note)

targets.question: Let my AI search the Hub, call Spaces, and push to my repos

pick.name: Hugging Face MCP Server

access.scope_note: Hosted at https://huggingface.co/mcp (hf.co/mcp). Auth is an HF token as a Bearer header, or OAuth via ?login; anonymous gets a standard read set plus an image generator. Read: hf_fs (one tool that walks repos, storage, docs, papers), model/dataset/paper/Space search, doc search, any Gradio Space tagged mcp-server. Write (logged in): 'Contribute Repos' creates repos and writes files to them; Jobs runs, monitors and schedules jobs on HF infra; Sandboxes creates compute sandboxes attached to buckets and repos. No delete tool is documented. Which tools you get is chosen per account at huggingface.co/settings/mcp, and that page generates the client config. Self-host with the MIT repo (stdio or streamable HTTP) if you want a fixed tool set.

pick.cost: Free. Jobs, Sandboxes and ZeroGPU Spaces draw on your account's paid compute or quota.
pick.the_catch: The tool set is a moving target. On 22 Jul 2026 HF replaced most search tools with hf_fs and added Sandboxes; anything you wrote against the old names broke. Your selection lives on a settings page, not in your config, so two people with the 'same' server get different tools. Repo writes use whatever token you paste; a classic write token can push to every repo you own, so mint a fine-grained one. Jobs and Sandboxes are billable compute the model can start on its own. The GitHub repo's last tag is v0.4.16 (Aug 2025) despite nearly a thousand commits; the hosted service is where releases actually land.

alternate.name: mcp-hfspace
alternate.maintainer: evalstate (community; author now works on the official server)

access.scope_note: Calls named Gradio Spaces (image generation, vision, TTS, chat) and handles file upload and download. Optional HF_TOKEN only for private Spaces or your own quota. No Hub writes.

alternate.cost: Free, MIT. Space usage draws on your ZeroGPU quota if you pass a token.
alternate.the_catch: The README says it has been superseded by the official server and Gradio's native MCP endpoints, and there has been no release since April 2025. Only worth it if you need a pinned, offline-configurable list of Spaces and refuse to use the hosted endpoint.

targets.avoid: None specifically; the official hosted server has absorbed the community options. Just do not paste a write-scoped classic token into any of them.

sources.label: HF blog: Building the HF MCP server

targets.question: Let my AI find and run image, video and audio models on Replicate

pick.name: Replicate MCP server

access.scope_note: Remote at https://mcp.replicate.com/sse (you paste a Replicate API token; Claude Code gets a browser flow). Local via npx replicate-mcp with REPLICATE_API_TOKEN. Replicate's docs say it 'supports all of the operations in Replicate's HTTP API': models.search/list/get, predictions.create/get, hardware, and the deployments and models management endpoints, which include delete and cancel. No read-only flag is documented; the only switch is --tools=all (default) or --tools=code, an alpha 'code mode' that gives the model two tools: search the SDK docs and execute TypeScript against the Replicate SDK in a sandbox. Token scope is the whole account.

pick.cost: Server is free. Every prediction is billed to your Replicate account at the model's per-second or per-output price.
pick.the_catch: There is no confirmation between 'the model decided to run this' and your card being charged. create_predictions is just another tool, and video models cost real money per call, so run it in a client that prompts before tool use, or set a spend limit on the account first. The tool surface is the entire HTTP API, deletes included. The npm stdio package (replicate-mcp 0.9.0) has not shipped since June 2025 even though the hosted endpoint got MCP Registry discovery in Feb 2026; treat the remote as the maintained one. Code mode is alpha and executes generated TypeScript.

targets.avoid: deepfates/mcp-replicate still tops search results. It was archived on 18 May 2026 and is read-only on GitHub; the author points at Replicate's official server.

targets.question: Let my AI search YouTube, read video stats, comments and transcripts

pick.name: mcp-youtube (@kirbah/mcp-youtube)

access.scope_note: Read-only against the YouTube Data API v3 with your own key (YOUTUBE_API_KEY). Tools: getVideoDetails, searchVideos, getTranscripts, getChannelStatistics, getChannelTopVideos, getTrendingVideos, getVideoCategories, getVideoComments, findConsistentOutlierChannels. No upload, edit, comment or playlist writes; an API key cannot act on your channel anyway, that needs OAuth which this server does not do. Optional MongoDB (MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING) caches responses and is required for the outlier tool.

pick.cost: Free, MIT. YouTube Data API is free up to Google's default 10,000 quota units a day.
pick.the_catch: Quota arithmetic. searchVideos costs 100 units and getChannelTopVideos 101, so the default project quota is about a hundred searches a day before every tool goes dark until midnight Pacific. The README's answer is to bolt on MongoDB caching, which is another thing to run. getTranscripts is '0 API cost' because it scrapes captions outside the official API; that path breaks whenever YouTube changes the page. And this is one person's project: nobody at Google is on the hook for it.

alternate.name: youtube-mcp-server

access.scope_note: Ten read tools: video get/search, transcript, channel get/search/list videos/find creators, playlist get/items. Takes up to three API keys (YOUTUBE_API_KEY, _KEY2, _KEY3) and rotates on quota exhaustion. Despite the repo blurb about 'video management' and 'Shorts creation', no upload, update or delete tool is documented.

alternate.cost: Free, MIT. Same 10,000-unit daily API quota per key.
alternate.the_catch: The description oversells it. It reads; it does not manage. Key rotation across three Google Cloud projects to dodge quota is the sort of thing Google's terms frown on. v1.0.2 in July 2026 fixed a transcript language parameter that had silently never been passed, which tells you how much testing the transcript path gets.

targets.avoid: anaisbetts/mcp-youtube: the most-starred one, but it only pulls subtitles via a locally installed yt-dlp, last release v0.6.0 in March 2025, and yt-dlp is in a permanent arms race with YouTube. Also note there is no official Google server: google/mcp lists Workspace, Maps, BigQuery and friends, not YouTube.

targets.question: Let my AI read and update records, tables and automations in my Airtable bases

pick.name: Airtable MCP server (hosted)

access.scope_note: Endpoint https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp. Around 40 tools: list/search/create/update/delete records, create/update/delete tables, create/update fields, create bases, build and delete interfaces and pages, create/update/delete automations, forms, comments, plus revert_action for eligible mutations. Access mirrors your Airtable role per base; commenters and read-only users get read only. Narrowable with a PAT limited to data.records:read and schema.bases:read. Enterprise admins can allowlist the integration and users can remove bases from the connection.

pick.cost: Free on all Airtable plans; calls count against normal API rate limits and base record limits.
pick.the_catch: The help centre still says delete is limited to inactive automations, but the tool reference lists delete_records_for_table, delete_table and delete_interface, and if you are a base Creator the AI inherits that. The OAuth scope set Airtable recommends includes schema.bases:write and data.records:write by default. Record creation is capped at 10 per call, so bulk loads crawl. Airtable says tool names 'may change', and its own CLI wrapper is labelled experimental.

alternate.name: airtable-mcp-server

access.scope_note: 16 tools: list_bases, list_tables, describe_table, list/search/get records, create_record, update_records, delete_records, create/update table, create/update field, comments. Runs locally over stdio via npx; HTTP mode exists but has no auth of its own. Minimum scopes are schema.bases:read and data.records:read, so a read-only PAT gives a read-only server. npm 1.14.0 published 2026-07-27. MIT.

alternate.cost: Free.
alternate.the_catch: The README warns HTTP mode has no built-in authentication and is open to DNS-rebinding from a browser tab; keep it on stdio or behind a proxy. No interfaces or automations support, which is most of the reason to use the official server.

pick.name: Exa MCP Server

targets.question: Let my AI fetch a URL and read it as markdown, with no API key or vendor

pick.name: Fetch MCP Server (mcp-server-fetch)

access.scope_note: One tool, fetch(url, max_length=5000, start_index, raw). Plain HTTP GET from wherever the server runs, converted to markdown, paged by start_index. No allow-list, no IP blocking: the README says it 'can access local/internal IP addresses'. Respects robots.txt for model-initiated requests only; --ignore-robots-txt turns that off. --user-agent and --proxy-url are the only other knobs. Python, stdio only: uvx mcp-server-fetch, pip, or the mcp/fetch Docker image.

Also: 5,000 characters per call by default, so reading a long page is many round trips, and JavaScript-rendered pages come back empty. targets.question: Let my AI drive a real browser: navigate, click, fill forms, read pages, take screenshots

pick.name: Playwright MCP

access.scope_note: Full browser control. 71 tools; 42 are marked read-only false (click, type, fill_form, file_upload, select, evaluate JavaScript, run_code_unsafe). Default mode is a persistent Chrome profile per workspace under ~/.cache/ms-playwright (or the OS equivalent) that keeps cookies and logins between sessions. --isolated keeps the profile in memory; --storage-state loads a saved cookie file into an isolated context; --extension attaches to your running Chrome or Edge through the Playwright Extension and uses your live logged-in tabs. File access is restricted to workspace roots unless --allow-unrestricted-file-access. Opt-in caps: vision, pdf, devtools, storage, network, testing, config. --allowed-origins / --blocked-origins filter requests but, per the README, do not affect redirects and are not a security boundary. --secrets masks values in tool output. No auth on the HTTP transport; --host 0.0.0.0 exposes it to the network.

pick.cost: Free, Apache-2.0. You run it (npx @playwright/mcp@latest, or the mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/mcp Docker image, headless Chromium only).
pick.the_catch: Whatever the browser is logged into, the model is logged into. The default persistent profile survives restarts, and --extension hands the agent your actual Chrome session: Gmail, GitHub, your bank, whatever tab is open, with no per-site consent. Any page it visits can prompt-inject it, and the origin filters explicitly do not follow redirects. browser_run_code_unsafe ships in the core set, enabled by default, and its own description says it is 'RCE-equivalent' in the server process; there is no flag to switch it off. Add --isolated for anything that reads untrusted pages, keep --extension for supervised one-offs, and never bind --host 0.0.0.0 without a network boundary. An SSRF report (issue #1626, May 2026) asking for RFC1918 and link-local blocking was closed without a fix: the browser will open 169.254.169.254 or your intranet if a page tells it to. Microsoft's own README now says coding agents should prefer playwright-cli over MCP for token cost.

alternate.name: Chrome DevTools MCP

access.scope_note: Drives Chrome over the DevTools protocol: 52 tools for input, navigation, screenshots, evaluate_script, console, network, performance traces, Lighthouse, heap snapshots. Launches its own Chrome with a persistent profile at ~/.cache/chrome-devtools-mcp/chrome-profile by default; --isolated for a throwaway one. --autoConnect (Chrome M144+) or --browserUrl attach to your running Chrome after you enable remote debugging at chrome://inspect, which gives the agent your logged-in sessions. Category flags (--categoryEmulation, --categoryPerformance, --categoryNetwork) trim tool groups. README: 'exposes content of the browser instance to the MCP clients allowing them to inspect, debug, and modify any data in the browser'.

alternate.cost: Free, Apache-2.0. Self-run via npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest; needs current stable Chrome and Node LTS.
alternate.the_catch: Attaching to your real Chrome means opening the remote debugging port, and the README warns any process on the machine can then connect and control the browser, not just the MCP client. Chrome only; no Firefox or WebKit. Better for performance and network debugging than for general browsing agents.

preamble.title: Before you connect anything
points: A server's tool descriptions are read by the model as instructions. A malicious or compromised server can hide directives in them — OWASP calls this tool poisoning.
A server you approved today can change what its tools do tomorrow. Approval is not a one-time event; pin versions where you can.
One server's output can steer another server's actions. A web page fetched by one tool can instruct the model to use a second tool with write access.
Default scopes are almost always wider than the job. Read-write is the norm; read-only is something you have to ask for, and often can't get.
Remote servers with OAuth are safer than pasting a live API key into a config file. Prefer them where the vendor offers one.

sources.label: Cloud Security Alliance — tool poisoning and IDE auto-execution
Microsoft — the state of MCP security in 2026

method.how: For each thing a builder might connect, we looked for a server maintained by the vendor itself. Where one exists it is the pick unless it is clearly worse. Access, auth and transport are read from the server's own README or docs, not assumed. 'Avoid' names servers that are widely recommended and either archived, unsafe by construction, or a wrapper of a wrapper.
method.tested_on: Not independently tested. Repos, docs and release pages were read on 2026-09-03. We did not install and run all 57.
method.conflicts: None. No affiliate links, no paid placements, no relationship with any vendor listed.
